difficultyRationale: A direct application of the happens-before rule for monitor lock/unlock, stated plainly in the JLS.
prompt: Thread A writes to several plain (non-volatile) fields inside a `synchronized(lock) { ... }` block, then exits the block, releasing `lock`. Thread B later enters its own `synchronized(lock) { ... }` block on the same `lock` object and reads those fields. Per the Java Language Specification, what guarantees Thread B sees Thread A's writes?
explanation: The JLS happens-before order includes a specific rule for monitors: an unlock action on a monitor happens-before every subsequent lock action on that same monitor. Because Thread A's writes occur before it unlocks, and Thread B's reads occur after it locks the same object, the happens-before relation chains the writes to the reads — no `volatile` or other modifier is needed on the individual fields.

options.text: The unlock of `lock` by Thread A happens-before the subsequent lock of the same `lock` by Thread B, so everything Thread A wrote before unlocking is visible to Thread B after it locks.
options.explanation: Correct: this is the JLS's monitor happens-before rule (§17.4.5) — unlock happens-before every subsequent lock on the same monitor, which transitively orders Thread A's writes before Thread B's reads.

options.text: Nothing extra is guaranteed; the fields would also need to be declared `volatile` for Thread B to reliably see the writes.
options.explanation: This gets the rule backwards: the monitor's own lock/unlock happens-before edge already supplies the ordering, which is exactly why synchronized blocks are a complete alternative to volatile for this purpose, not a supplement to it.

options.text: The guarantee only holds if both threads happen to run on the same CPU core.
options.explanation: The happens-before guarantee is a property of the Java Memory Model's synchronization actions, independent of which core or core affinity a thread is scheduled on; the JVM's lock implementation is responsible for making it hold across cores.

options.text: The JVM only guarantees visibility for fields declared `final` that are set during construction and never mutated afterward; ordinary mutable fields modified inside a synchronized block are not covered by this rule.
options.explanation: Final-field semantics (§17.5) are a separate, narrower guarantee for safe construction. The monitor happens-before rule in §17.4.5 is general-purpose and applies to any field written before an unlock and read after the matching lock, mutable or not.

references.title: Java Language Specification, SE 21 — Chapter 17: Threads and Locks (§17.4.5, Happens-before Order)
